name: Rumi Darwaza
summary: The Rumi Darwaza (sometimes known as the Turkish Gate), in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, is a gateway which was built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784.
presentContext: It is an example of Awadhi architecture.

facts.claim: The Rumi Darwaza (sometimes known as the Turkish Gate), in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, is a gateway which was built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784.
facts.supportingExcerpt: The Rumi Darwaza (sometimes known as the Turkish Gate), in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, is a gateway which was built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784.

facts.claim: It is an example of Awadhi architecture.
facts.supportingExcerpt: It is an example of Awadhi architecture.

facts.claim: The Rumi Darwaza is sixty feet tall and was modeled after the Sublime Porte in Istanbul.
facts.supportingExcerpt: The Rumi Darwaza is sixty feet tall and was modeled after the Sublime Porte in Istanbul.

facts.claim: It is adjacent to the Asafi Imambara, Teele Wali Masjid and used to mark the entrance to Old Lucknow.
facts.supportingExcerpt: It is adjacent to the Asafi Imambara, Teele Wali Masjid and used to mark the entrance to Old Lucknow.

facts.claim: When the city grew and expanded, it was used as an entrance to a palace which was later demolished by the British Raj following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
facts.supportingExcerpt: When the city grew and expanded, it was used as an entrance to a palace which was later demolished by the British Raj following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
